title: Converting Fractions to Decimals
seo_title: Grade 7 Converting Fractions to Decimals Worksheets: Terminating and Repeating Decimals
standard_text: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 fractions to decimals worksheets: divide to convert, terminating and repeating decimals, bar notation, negative and mixed numbers, decimals back to fractions, comparing and ordering, and word problems. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: Divide the numerator by the denominator. The decimal ends or repeats.
body_html:
A fraction is a division

To change a fraction to a decimal, divide the numerator by the denominator. Use long division and keep adding zeros. The decimal either ends (terminates) or a group of digits repeats forever.

FractionDivideDecimalType
121 ÷ 20.5terminates
383 ÷ 80.375terminates
232 ÷ 30.6repeats
161 ÷ 60.16repeats
2112 ÷ 110.18repeats

Bar notation

Draw a bar over the digits that repeat: 0.1666… = 0.16 and 0.181818… = 0.18. In simplest form, a fraction terminates only when its denominator has no prime factors except 2 and 5.

Example

Write 512 as a decimal.

5 ÷ 12 = 0.41666…

The 6 repeats, so put the bar over the 6 only.

Answer: 0.416

Example

Write −2 34 as a decimal.

34 = 3 ÷ 4 = 0.75.

Keep the whole number and the sign.

Answer: −2.75

Common mistakes

  • Dividing the wrong way: 38 is 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375, not 8 ÷ 3.
  • Writing the digits side by side: 38 is not 0.38.
  • Putting the bar over too many digits: 0.1666… is 0.16, not 0.16.

faq.q: How do you convert a fraction to a decimal?
faq.a: Divide the numerator by the denominator. 3/8 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375.
A decimal in which a digit or group of digits repeats forever, like 2/3 = 0.666… or 2/11 = 0.181818…

faq.q: How do I know if a fraction terminates?
faq.a: Write it in simplest form. If the denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5, the decimal terminates. Otherwise it repeats.

faq.q: How do you write bar notation?
faq.a: Draw a bar over only the digits that repeat. 0.1666… is written 0.16 with the bar over the 6 only.

items.q: Which shows 0.272727… with bar notation?
items.e: The block 27 repeats, so the bar goes over both digits.

items.q: Which shows 0.1666… with bar notation?

items.q: What does 0.3 mean?
items.e: The bar means the digits under it repeat forever. 0.3 = 1/3.

items.q: Which fraction equals 0.6?
items.e: 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666… = 0.6. 3/5 and 6/10 are 0.6 exactly.
